summary: Configured PostgreSQL 15 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on RHEL9. Built a dedicated CA on node1, issued per-node server certs (with SAN) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator), distributed via SSH. All three nodes run PostgreSQL with ssl=on and the CA as trust root. pg_hba.conf on every node restricts the `replication` database to `hostssl ... cert clientcert=verify-full` for the `replicator` role from the cluster subnet, with an explicit `hostnossl replication all reject` fallback, so only TLS connections presenting a certificate issued by this CA are accepted. Standbys were bootstrapped via pg_basebackup -R over verify-full mutual TLS, producing correct primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and the client cert/key. Verified: (a) replication streams over TLS 1.3 with client cert CN=replicator recognized, (b) writes on node1 replicate to node2/node3, (c) a request without a client cert is rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate'), (d) a cert signed by a different, untrusted CA is rejected at the TLS handshake ('unknown ca'), (e) plaintext replication attempts are rejected by pg_hba. Then executed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured a boot-id baseline and healthy replication baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node2 then node3 (standbys) and finally node1 (primary) one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed PostgreSQL, recovery status, replication streaming (still TLS-encrypted with correct cipher), and full data consistency recovered on each node before moving to the next.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 15.18 (AppStream module) on node1, node2, node3
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes
Generated a dedicated CA (CN=pg-replication-ca) on node1
Issued SAN-bearing server certs for node1/node2/node3 and a client cert CN=replicator, all signed by the CA
Distributed CA cert and per-node/client certs to node2 and node3 via SSH using the cluster keypair
Initialized node1 as primary (postgresql-setup --initdb), configured ssl on with the issued cert/key/CA, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, created replicator role
Configured pg_hba.conf on all nodes to require hostssl + cert clientcert=verify-full for replication by the replicator role, with hostnossl reject fallback
Bootstrapped node2 and node3 via pg_basebackup -R over sslmode=verify-full mutual TLS against node1, producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo with client cert auth
Installed per-node server certs and TLS config on node2/node3, started them as hot standbys
Verified replication streaming state, TLS cipher/version, and client cert DN/issuer on the primary
Verified live data replication node1 -> node2/node3
Negative-tested: connection without client cert rejected; connection with cert from an untrusted CA rejected; plaintext replication rejected
Captured boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes
Sequentially restarted node2, then node3, then node1 via systemctl reboot, polling for reconnect and confirming changed boot_id each time
Verified PostgreSQL, recovery state, TLS-streaming replication, and full data consistency recovered after each restart

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL installed with node1 as primary, node2/node3 as standbys
evidence.summary: PostgreSQL 15.18 installed on all nodes; node1 initialized and started as writable primary.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated CA created for the cluster; per-node and client certs issued by it
evidence.summary: CA (CN=pg-replication-ca) generated on node1; server certs for node1/node2/node3 with SANs and a replicator client cert signed by the CA.

pg_stat_replication joined with pg_stat_ssl shows both standbys connected via TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, with client_dn=/CN=replicator and issuer_dn=/CN=pg-replication-ca, both before and after the primary's restart.

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: Replication attempt with no client cert rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate'); attempt with a cert from an unrelated CA rejected at TLS handshake ('unknown ca'); plaintext (non-SSL) replication attempt rejected by pg_hba ('rejects replication connection ... no encryption').
Row inserted on node1 primary observed on both node2 and node3 standbys, which report pg_is_in_recovery=true.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: node1 boot_id baseline 98aa35f5...; reboot acked; boot_id changed to e16595db... after polling; post-restart primary is not in recovery, both standbys reconnected over TLS, and a new write replicated to both standbys.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: node2 boot_id baseline f1afbc7f...; reboot acked; boot_id changed to 89a8e55d...; postgresql active, in recovery, existing data intact, and primary shows it streaming again after a fresh insert.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: node3 boot_id baseline b634b53f...; reboot acked; boot_id changed to 85d9c034...; postgresql active, in recovery, and caught up with all rows including the one written during node2's restart window.
